advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER can only be set in genuine test-worker processes, or add a corroborating pytest-context signal before routing gates into the isolated slot namespace, so a leaked/inherited env var cannot silently disable the host-global cap for a real gate run.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/gate_admission.py:149 `worker = resolve_pytest_xdist_worker()` then `if not worker: return None` — the ONLY discriminator between the operator namespace and an isolated namespace is the presence of PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER
src/rebar/_config_resolvers.py:107 `resolve_pytest_xdist_worker` reads `os.environ.get("PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER")` with no verification that the process is genuinely a pytest worker
ABSENCE: no assertion or guard that the process is actually under pytest (e.g. sys.modules check) — a stray/inherited env var alone flips a production concurrency bound off silently
advisory.finding: Any real (non-test) rebar gate process that runs with PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER present in its environment — e.g. a gate subprocess spawned by a test, or an env var leaked into an operator shell — will silently route into a worker-scoped slot namespace and thereby escape the host-global concurrency cap the guard exists to enforce.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting the reciprocal isolation direction: an operator gate is admitted while an xdist worker (PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER=gw0) holds the cap, proving the worker does not consume operator host slots.
evidence: docs/config.md: 'so `make verify` does not consume — or get starved by — the operator-facing host slots'

tests/unit/test_gate_admission_09da.py:117-120 — with ga.gate_admission("plan_review", "operator-gate", root): ... setenv PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER gw0 ... with ga.gate_admission("plan_review", "pytest-worker-gate", root): pass
ABSENCE: no test holds a worker-scoped slot (PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER set, cap=1) and then asserts an operator gate (env unset) is still admitted; only the worker-not-starved direction is covered.
advisory.finding: The docs contract for the change is bidirectional ('does not consume — or get starved by' the operator host slots), but the only new test asserts a single direction: a worker gate is admitted while an operator holds the cap (worker not starved). The reciprocal behavior — an operator gate is still admitted while an xdist worker holds a slot (worker does not consume operator capacity) — is enabled by the added _slot_dir namespace redirect yet has no assertion.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a mirror test: set PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER=gw0, enter ga.gate_admission for a worker gate against gate_host(1); then delenv PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER and assert an operator gate_admission is admitted (no GateCongestedError).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Cover the worker-id sanitization branch by driving _test_slot_namespace with a worker id containing a non-alnum character and asserting the resulting namespace is sanitized.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/gate_admission.py:152 — safe = "".join(char if char.isalnum() or char in {"-", "_"} else "_" for char in worker)
tests/unit/test_gate_admission_09da.py:118 — monkeypatch.setenv("PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER", "gw0") (an all-alnum id that never exercises the replacement branch)
ABSENCE: no test sets PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER to a value with a special character to cover the else-branch of the sanitizer.
advisory.finding: The newly added worker-id sanitization branch (replacing non-alphanumeric characters with '_') is untested; no test supplies a worker id containing a character that triggers the replacement path.
